blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Provably secure linguistic steganography assumes that the receiver recovers the sender's tokens, but a text channel delivers only text, and ambiguous tokenizations break extraction. Existing fixes change the distribution, synchronize whole pools of tokens at a capacity that collapses with large vocabularies, or track several token histories. We prove that if extraction is exact and error-free across full-support language models, a single-history receiver is confined to a prefix-free candidate set at every step -- even if it reads the entire future text and the sender constrains later steps -- and must therefore give up the stop entropy, the entropy of deciding whether each prefix token ends there. Fixing these stop decisions on the prefix forest with shared randomness yields coin projection: a closed-form scheme that attains the bound, works with any distribution coder in one model call per token, preserves ordinary sampling, and refines SyncPool for every key. Across English, Chinese and Japanese, ambiguous text is rare (at most 11 in 1,000 tokens), yet the stop entropy at word and morpheme prefixes takes 7.2-9.0% of the entropy at every step; SyncPool's further loss comes from space and single-byte UTF-8 hubs that merge subtrees while carrying almost no stop uncertainty. Coin projection keeps 91-93% of the string entropy for the coder at every vocabulary size; with the full vocabulary, it turns 2.16-6.85 times as much entropy into message bits as SyncPool and recovers every completed message.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Provably secure linguistic steganography hides a message in text sampled from a language model.
The stegotext then follows the model’s own distribution, and no warden without the key can tell it from ordinary output ( Hopper et al., 2002 ; Ziegler et al., 2019 ; Kaptchuk et al., 2021 ; de Witt et al., 2023 ; Ding et al., 2023 ) .
The coders behind these schemes assume that the receiver recovers the sender’s tokens.
Real channels carry text, however, and one text admits many tokenizations.
When the receiver retokenizes, it can recover a different sequence; with 7B models, 5–10% of 128-bit messages are lost ( Yan and Murawaki, 2025 ) .

当接收器重现时,它可以恢复不同的序列;使用7B模型,128位消息的5-10%丢失(Yan和Murawaki,2025).

blocks.en:
Existing fixes pay for disambiguation in one of three ways. Filters remove candidates so that the text parses uniquely ( Nozaki and Murawaki, 2022 ; Yan et al., 2023 ; Yan and Murawaki, 2025 ) .
They thereby change the distribution that security rests on. SyncPool keeps the distribution exact by encoding pools of prefix-related tokens ( Qi et al., 2025 ) .
A single short token, however, can be a byte prefix of most candidates; the bare space is a prefix of nearly every English word token.
The pools then merge, and capacity collapses as the vocabulary grows.
On Llama-3.2 with the full vocabulary, SyncPool’s coder sees only 14% of the entropy ( Section 3 ). Multi-history schemes recover nearly all the entropy, but they call the model on several tokenizations at every step ( Feng et al., 2025 ) .

Our contributions are as follows. • A tight single-history bound. Across full-support language models, any exact, error-free scheme with a single-history receiver is confined to prefix-free candidate sets at every step—even if the receiver reads the whole text and the sender constrains later steps—and embeds at most H str − H stop H_{\mathrm{str}}-H_{\mathrm{stop}} bits per step; reaching equality allows randomizing only end-of-token decisions ( Theorems 1 and 2 ). • Coin projection. Realizing those stop decisions on the prefix forest gives a closed-form scheme that attains the bound, works with any distribution coder in one model call per token, keeps the law of ordinary sampling, and refines SyncPool for every key ( Section 4.1 ). • Orthographic hubs versus lexical prefixes. Although at most 11 tokens in 1,000 are tokenized non-canonically, H stop H_{\mathrm{stop}} stays at 7.2–9.0% of the entropy across scripts and vocabulary sizes because it comes from complete words, stems and particles that can either stand alone or take a continuation; the bare space and single-byte UTF-8 prefixes merge whole subtrees yet rarely end a token, inflating only the branch entropy that SyncPool gives up ( Section 3 ).

blocks.en:
Sender and receiver share a secret key K K and a context.
At step t t , the language model gives a token law π t \pi_{t} on the history, truncated to the top k k tokens for a public k k .

blocks.en:
Beyond Section 2 , Yan et al. (2024) verify candidates against the history, Yan and Murawaki (2025) measure inconsistency rates and note the lack of theory, and Yan et al. (2026a) list high capacity under provable security as open.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
A single-history receiver must pay the stop entropy H stop H_{\mathrm{stop}} of ambiguous word and morpheme prefixes in the candidate pool, even when ambiguous text is rare; coin projection pays nothing more and preserves whitespace and UTF-8 hub trees for the coder.
On English, Chinese and Japanese, it keeps 91–93% of string entropy even at full vocabularies, giving 2.16–6.85 × \times SyncPool’s utilization at zero divergence and zero error.

在英文、中文和日文方面,它保留了91–93%的弦形,即使在满分字节时也是如此,给出了2.16–6.85×\times Syncpool的利用率零分和零出错。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our bound covers online schemes that keep a single history, never fail, and are exact across all full-support language models ( Appendix A ).
It is the price of this universality across models: a scheme that needs exactness only for models whose non-canonical continuations are rare can pay less ( Appendix A ).
In the extreme, a model that places no mass on non-canonical encodings ( Vieira et al., 2025b ) makes canonical retokenization exact; making a deployed model canonical, however, changes the law that the stegotext must match.
Likewise, relaxing token-level exactness to text-level exactness across full-support models does not raise the single-history budget when the sender is online along a single history ( Appendix A ); exceeding H str − H stop H_{\mathrm{str}}-H_{\mathrm{stop}} via text-level exactness requires the sender to query alternative tokenizations of the text.
blocks.zh:
我们的捆绑覆盖了保持单一历史、永不失败的在线计划,并且精确地涵盖所有完全支持的语言模式(附录A)。
这种普遍性在各种模式中的代价是:一种只需要准确性的计划,对于那些非卡通性的延续很少的模型,可以少花钱(附录A)。
在极端情况下,不给非卡通编码造成质量的模型(维埃拉等,2025年b)使卡通复刻精确;然而,使部署的克通模型改变stegotext必须匹配的定律.
同样地,在全支持模式中将符号级精确度放宽到文本级精确度并不能提高单历史预算,当发送者沿着单一历史线在线(附录A)时;超过H str – H stop H_{\mathrm{str}}-H_{\mathrm{stop}}通过文本级精确度要求发送者查询文本的替代符号.

blocks.en:
Coin projection still pays H stop H_{\mathrm{stop}} , 7.2–9.0% of the entropy in our measurements.
Exceeding it requires multiple histories or a nonzero divergence.

blocks.en:
Like every provably secure scheme, the receiver needs the model.
With the full vocabulary, our CPU implementation of the projection takes 28.0 ms per step on English, against 17.8 ms for the forward pass of the 3B model.
Bit-exact agreement between sender and receiver relies on a fixed computation order.
blocks.zh:
和每个可以证明安全的计划一样,接收者需要模型.
有了完整的词汇,我们的CPU执行投影在英语上每步需要28.0ms,而3B模型的前传需要17.8ms.
发送方和接收方之间的比特精确协议依赖于固定的计算顺序.

blocks.en:
Exactness here is a property of the law handed to the coder.
The arithmetic coder still rounds probabilities, and Cao et al. (2026a) detect arithmetic-coding and Meteor stegotext from the low-probability tokens that rounding removes.
This concerns the coder rather than disambiguation and applies equally to every method we compare; coin projection can feed any coder that closes this gap.
Our divergence is likewise a per-step quantity: every compared method stops the text once the message is complete, and we do not analyze what the resulting length reveals.
blocks.zh:
这里的准确性是交给编码员的法律财产.
算术编码器仍能回转概率,而曹等(2026a)从四舍五入去除的低概率符号中检测出算术编码和Meteor stegotext.
这与编码器有关,而不是混淆不清,同样适用于我们所比较的每一种方法;硬币投影可以给任何能缩小这一差距的编码器提供素材.
我们的分歧同样是逐个步骤的数量:每个比较方法在信息完成后就停止文本,我们不分析由此产生的长度显示的内容。

blocks.en:
Our models have 3–4B parameters, and we cover three languages and two tokenizer families.
Larger models of these families share their tokenizers, so the prefix forest and its hub tokens stay the same and only the next-token law changes; the forward-only prediction of Section 5.3 estimates the gain for such a model from its forward passes, but we have not measured extraction end to end beyond 4B.
blocks.zh:
我们的模型有3–4B参数,我们覆盖了三种语言和两种活化剂家庭。
这些家庭的更大模型共享了它们的活化剂,所以前缀森林及其中心标志保持不变,只有下缀的法则变化;第5.3节的前缀预测估计了这种模型从其前缀中产生的收益,但我们还没有测量出取出结束到4B后.

blocks.en: Ethics Statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en:
Steganography protects private communication, and it can also hide harmful content.
Our method does not make stegotext easier to produce than existing provably secure schemes; it makes extraction reliable.
We will release code for research use.
blocks.zh:
Steganography保护了私人通信,它也可以隐藏有害的内容.
我们的方法并不使Stegotext比现有的可证明安全的办法更容易生产;它使提取变得可靠。
我们将发布代码供研究使用。

The channel carries only the continuation as a Unicode string.
With byte-level tokenizers, the arithmetic coder can resolve all 128 message bits at a token boundary that lies inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character.
Whenever the coder interval resolves the message at step t t but the concatenated output bytes are not yet valid UTF-8, the sender continues encoding the same message integer for at most 8 additional steps until the byte stream ends on a valid UTF-8 character boundary.
Because these trailing steps encode the same integer, the receiver’s arithmetic decoder replays them without altering the recovered 128-bit message.
A text whose bytes are still not valid UTF-8—for example when full-vocabulary byte-level sampling emits an unpaired mid-stream byte—cannot be sent as a Unicode string, so its message counts as unfinished, for every method alike (1 SyncPool text at the full vocabulary on English).
At both ends we set clean_up_tokenization_spaces=False ; otherwise, HuggingFace’s default decoder rewrites punctuation sequences such as “ ␣, ” and invalidates canonical retokenization even when no tokenization ambiguity occurred.

该频道仅作为Unicode字符串载续作.
用字节级的活化器,算术编码器可以在一个位于多字节UTF-8字符内的活化边界上解析出所有128个消息比特.

blocks.en:
Across the 1800 Native messages in Table 2 (600 per language), 88 completed messages fail to decode (19 on English, 21 on Chinese and 48 on Japanese; Table 9 ), and 2 more Japanese messages do not finish within 512 tokens.
Every failed extraction falls into one of three disjoint categories: • Silent wrong bits (48 of 88, 55%). Every retokenized token lies inside the candidate pool at its step, so the arithmetic decoder terminates cleanly and returns 128 bits that do not match the sender’s message.
Without an external integrity tag, the receiver cannot tell that desynchronization occurred and therefore cannot request retransmission.
At the full vocabulary, candidate-pool membership never fails, so every Native failure that is not a prompt-boundary merge is silent (3, 2 and 7 on English, Chinese and Japanese). • Out-of-pool aborts (26 of 88). Canonical retokenization merges or splits emitted bytes into a token outside the top- k k candidate pool at that step, halting the decoder.
These failures shrink as k k grows and vanish at the full vocabulary. • Prompt-boundary merges (14 of 88). When the continuation does not begin with a whitespace delimiter, the tokenizer can merge the trailing characters of the prompt with the opening bytes of the continuation.
Tokenizing the continuation alone recovers 7 of 12 such cases on Chinese; the remaining 5 Chinese cases and all 9 Japanese cases (where SentencePiece prepends ‘ ’ on standalone strings) remain unrecoverable. Coin projection, SyncPool, Stepwise, MWIS, Basic and hub-drop all achieve zero extraction errors across every completed message.

blocks.en:
Single-history schemes evaluate the language model only on prefixes of the sender’s emitted token sequence X < t X_{<t} .
By Corollary 2 , their per-step coder budget cannot exceed H str − H stop H_{\mathrm{str}}-H_{\mathrm{stop}} .
Multi-history schemes such as LAS ( Feng et al., 2025 ) instead keep several weighted candidate token histories consistent with the visible text and query the model on more than one of them per step.
